subsenses.definition: (US law enforcement slang) To trick a suspect into entering a jurisdiction in which they can be lawfully arrested.
(US military slang) To transfer a serviceman against their will.

senses.definition: (transitive) To commandeer, hijack, or otherwise (usually wrongfully) appropriate a place or thing.
examples: Let's see if we can shanghai a room for a couple of hours.

senses.definition: (often capitalized, dated) A breed of chicken with large bodies, long legs, and feathered shanks.

examples: The ‘shanghai’ is the glaring daub required by some frame-makers for cheap auctions. They are turned out at so much by the day's labor, or at from $12 to $24 a dozen, by the piece.

senses.definition: (darts, often capitalized) A kind of dart game in which players are gradually eliminated ("shanghaied"), usually either by failing to reach a certain score in 3 quick throws or during a competition to hit a certain prechosen number and then be the first to hit the prechosen numbers of the other players.
examples: The hot twenty—including local favourites George Simmons, Tony Brown, Mick Norris and Lew Walker—have to sweat through nineteen 501s, one 1,001, one 2,001, one round-the-board-on-doubles, one shanghai and one halve-it.

quotes.text: ‘Shanghai’ may be played by teams of 8, in pairs, individually, or, in fact, any number.
